objective: Find an FP16/BF16-only local provider or bounded derivative for a true single-kernel B29 SwiGLU MLP: two input GEMMs, the accepted FP16 roundtrip and fast SwiGLU, then the complete K1152 down GEMM with beta-one residual.

target.activation: FP16 projection roundtrip followed by accepted fast SwiGLU

retained_graph_context.parent_stage: Stage08 id70 Q/K/V auxiliary-stream dependency DAG
retained_graph_context.observation: The accepted no-AB12 input projection plus SwiGLU remains an exposed hotspot, while linear2 remains a separate large library GEMM. This audit asks whether deleting their global intermediate is locally implementable, not whether either standalone GEMM can be retiled again.

intermediate_value.interpretation: Eliminating the tensor removes one full logical write and read, but the two-stream 48.24 MB working set fits in B300's 132.64 MB L2. Therefore 48.24 MB is an upper bound on memory-system traffic saved per FFN, not a DRAM-saving claim; input/down GEMM compute remains.

arithmetic_work.note: A fusion that recomputes the two input projections once for each of three N128 down-output tiles would triple the 18.52 GFLOP input stage and erase the memory-roundtrip value.

provider_inventory.finding: Computes two parallel GEMMs sharing X and an elementwise SiLU-multiply result. It does not consume that result in a second sequential GEMM; it is the same boundary already implemented more efficiently by the accepted no-AB12 SM103 kernel.

This is a genuine sequential single-kernel GEMM0-to-GEMM1 seed, but block residency requires threadblock_tile_N=problem_N; RF residency additionally requires warp_tile_N=threadblock_tile_N. It is implemented for SM75/80, not tcgen05/SM103.
provider_inventory.classification: true historical seed, major port and inapplicable shape contract

provider_inventory.finding: Merge/fork PipelineGroup primitives coordinate one GEMM's load, MMA, residual, activation, and store tasks. No tutorial makes one GEMM's distributed output the K-reduction input of another GEMM.

structural_blocker.statement: The down GEMM output tile depends on all 1152 activated hidden channels, while the input projection is partitioned across many hidden-N CTAs. An epilogue cannot hand one local hidden tile to a complete down-GEMM K reduction without either recomputation, cross-CTA exchange, or materialization.

cutlass_b2b_constraint_application.result: A single M128x1152 FP16 intermediate tile already exceeds B300 shared memory before weights, pipelines, barriers, or down accumulators; RF residency is still less feasible.

naive_output_tile_recomputation.effect: Each output CTA would recompute both complete input projections unless hidden chunks are exchanged, tripling the input-stage work from 18.52 to 55.57 GFLOP per FFN.

structural_blocker.single_owner_alternative: One persistent CTA/cluster could own an M tile, loop over hidden-K chunks, round each pair to FP16, apply SwiGLU into a shared-memory chunk, and accumulate all N384 down outputs in TMEM. This requires a new dual-mainloop pipeline, partial TMEM allocation, down-weight staging, and either one CTA owning N384 or DSM/cluster multicast. No audited provider implements it.
structural_blocker.numeric_constraint: The accepted projection FP32-to-FP16 roundtrip must occur before fast SwiGLU and before the down GEMM consumes each hidden chunk; directly feeding FP32 accumulators would repeat the already-rejected numerical implementation error.

native_abi_audit.existing_first_stage_c_abi: The accepted cuDNN OSS derivative has an authenticated CuTe-generated C wrapper for input projection plus SwiGLU only.
native_abi_audit.other_interfaces: Quack, Liger, FlashAttention fused_dense, Triton, and TileLang expose Python/Torch/JIT interfaces or old CUTLASS C++ device examples, not an SM103a full-MLP native ABI.

major_kernel_seeds: CUTLASS example 13 block/RF-resident B2B concept, after replacing its impossible N1152 residency contract
CuTe task-scheduling PipelineGroup primitives for a newly designed chunked producer-consumer mainloop
Triton or TileLang only as implementation languages, not reusable schedules

decision.reason: No provider crosses the dependent K1152 reduction boundary. The only true B2B example requires an impossible whole-N hidden tile, while all production-named MLP paths still materialize postact. A correct candidate would be a new persistent/cluster MLP algorithm, not a bounded provider swap.
reopen_conditions: A provider publishes an SM100/SM103 sequential GEMM fusion whose first GEMM may have N larger than its threadblock tile and whose second K reduction consumes distributed producer tiles without a full global intermediate
or a new design supplies static TMEM/SMEM/register accounting for the exact M10469/K384/H1152/N384 problem and proves no input-projection recomputation across down-output tiles

the design must preserve the FP16 projection boundary, fast SwiGLU semantics, beta-one residual, a stable native C ABI, and show an isolated complete-boundary advantage before any whole-graph GPU gate
